title: What If a Giant Iceberg Ran Aground Near 2 Million Penguins?

scenes.text: What if an iceberg the size of Long Island parked next to two million penguins?
That's A23a: about 3,100 square kilometers. It broke off Antarctica in 1986 and sat stuck on the seabed for decades.
In 2025 it drifted north and ran aground about 100 kilometers off South Georgia, home to over 2 million penguins.
A berg in the wrong spot can force penguins to travel several hundred extra miles to find food.
Its meltwater can also change the temperature and saltiness of the sea around it.
But here's the twist: melting bergs can release nutrients that feed ocean life. The full impact is still unclear.
